policy.description: Blocking line-coverage ratchets. Update measured counts in the same reviewed change whenever scope or coverage advances; never lower a floor without an explicit, justified scope change.

tolerance.rationale: The #369 body-observer ownership fix adds one instrumented and covered client/core line so stale handles compare their exact subscriber identity before cleanup, advancing the reviewed high-water from 2326/2666 (87.247%) to 2327/2667 (87.252%). Two clean Node 22.20/V8 runs on 2026-07-27 each passed all 1788 tests across 233 files and reproduced exactly 2327/2667. Retaining the existing one-line tolerance makes the minimum 2326/2667 (87.214%), stricter than the prior 2325/2666 tolerated floor (87.209%). coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact below-floor, above-baseline, scope-change, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.

EP-01.2 (#505) adds the one Platform v1 error envelope and per-request correlation ids: PlatformError, the enumerated PlatformErrorCode set, PlatformCorrelation, PlatformResults and PlatformRequestFilter, moving the instrumented scope from 36,251 to 36,336 lines. Every added line is exercised. PlatformErrorEnvelopeTests golden-pins the serialized envelope, pins the complete code set with each code's single status and its retryability, and asserts that an invented code throws rather than reaching the wire; PlatformCorrelationTests proves the id is stable within a request, differs between requests, is opaque lowercase hex, round-trips into both the X-Correlation-Id response header and the ILogger scope the action writes under, is never taken from a caller-supplied header, and that an unhandled exception becomes the envelope while its message, type and stack stay server-side. The authorization boundary is asserted structurally: PlatformRequestFilter implements only the action and exception filter interfaces and none of the authorization or resource ones, so 401/403 short-circuit before it runs and keep the zero-byte bodies EP-00 measured. Nine clean .NET 10.0.9/Coverlet runs on 2026-07-28 each passed all 2,366 tests at the same 36,336-line scope and measured 27,627 covered lines four times, 27,628 twice, and 27,629, 27,626 and 27,623 once each, so the reviewed high-water is 27,629 (76.038%) over an observed Coverlet spread of six lines. The six-line tolerance puts the floor at exactly the observed minimum of 27,623/36,336 (76.021%), stricter than the prior 27,539/36,251 tolerated floor (75.954%) in both line count and percentage. The high-water is the largest figure actually measured rather than a rounded-up margin, which is why it was raised twice while sampling: this gate rejects measurements above the baseline as well as below it, so the baseline has to be the real maximum for CI to be stable. coverage-baseline.test.js retains the exact scope-drift, regression, stale-baseline, and broad-tolerance negative boundaries.
